newsitem.title: USA: Dominican could face death penalty.
newsitem.headline: Dominican could face death penalty.

text.p: The U.S. government is considering whether to seek the death penalty in a murder and drug case against one of the first Dominicans to be extradited here in several decades, a federal prosecutor said Thursday.
The comment was made during the arraignment of Francisco Medina, 30, who is known by several aliases, including "Freddy Krueger" after the villain in a series of horror movies.
Medina and another Dominican, Maximo Reyes, 37, were extradited to New York on Wednesday in separate drug and murder cases.

Medina, who was arrested by Dominican police in April, is charged in a lengthy indictment accusing him of drug trafficking and more than a dozen violent murders in New York. Authorities allege he was an enforcer for a vicious drug gang called the Wild Cowboys involved in the distribution of crack cocaine and heroin in Manhattan and the Bronx.
Reyes, who was arrested in May, is accused of being a co-leader of another violent drug group called the Company that operates in Brooklyn.

During Medina's arraignment in Manhattan federal court, Assistant U.S. Attorney Thomas Arena said one of the charges against the defendant would allow the government to seek the death penalty. He said that the Justice Department and the U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of New York are evaluating the matter.
The United States has had an extradition treaty with the Dominican Republic since 1910, but a law passed by the Dominican legislature in 1969 barred the extradition of Dominican nationals.

Labe Richman, who was appointed by the court on Thursday to represent Medina, said he would investigate Medina's claim that his arrest was illegal because of the 1969 law and that his seizure amounted to kidnapping.
